purpose: Non-windowed verification of Rust regular workspace transition policy and compilation of a presentation-gated Metal overlay; native runtime acceptance deferred
build_consistency: final Ninja dry run reported no work to do
unit_verified_mechanisms: Rust owns regular transition eligibility for known distinct workspace indexes, visible sidebar, enabled animation and no reduced motion. It supplies the established +/-32 point displacement and 180ms duration; non-adjacent index changes retain the same displacement.

The complete previous Rust display-list, viewport, gesture and preview-content test set remains green. Shared scene capture keeps workspace IDs, browser commands and font metrics in the native application adapter.
implemented_pending_runtime_verification: Normal click/shortcut switches have a visual-only Metal viewport overlay using the same scene-data capture adapter as gesture previews, the established Rust display list and the shared GPU device/queue/pipeline. The successful path does not rasterize native row snapshots or use a Views compositor animation clock.

Before the first submission, the surface registers an MTLDrawable addPresentedHandler. Presentation posts a one-shot callback to the UI sequence, then starts the cached drawable translation through Core Animation. No synchronous GPU wait or polling timer is added.

A retained CAAnimationDelegate posts animation completion to the UI sequence. Normal completion removes the overlay, invalidates native fallback rows and schedules restoration of the ordinary Metal sidebar.

Generation guards reject stale presentation/completion callbacks after replacement, disable, hide or teardown. Window/sidebar reflow cancels a captured overlay instead of retaining old screen-space clipping.

Native row traversal is suppressed while a Metal gesture or normal transition owns the viewport. Overlay removal explicitly invalidates rows for fresh missing-drawable fallback. Header/footer input, focus/AX and browser/profile commands remain native adapters.
If the GPU overlay cannot prepare, it is discarded and the existing native layer animation runs. The default Views backend retains its existing native animation policy.
The compiled GUI case warms two real workspaces, checks target Unicode scene text, completion and normal Metal return, disable, rapid replacement, hide and window resize. It has not been executed.
deferred_checkpoint: Run the curated 45-case Metal matrix (prior 43 plus SwipePreviewUsesMetalWithoutNativeSnapshots and WorkspaceSwitchUsesPresentedMetalSceneAndCancels) and all 17 Views controls against the matching rebuilt sources.

Check actual drawable presentation ordering, Core Animation completion/cancellation, unavailable drawable/context fallback, repeated switches before first presentation, window hide/resize/teardown and reduced motion.

Inspect gesture and regular transitions with source scroll, Unicode, deep/collapsed folders, split pairs, focus/accessibility and multiple scales, then package/sign and inspect the matching isolated app.
Measure real-workload CPU, GPU and actual presentation separately. A presented callback is a lifecycle gate here, not a recorded benchmark or proof of speedup.
limitations: Compilation and non-windowed unit tests do not prove native Metal/CA behavior, visual quality, callback ordering, focus/AX behavior or performance. Those remain unaccepted until the GUI checkpoint.
The scene is a short-lived snapshot during the transition; native Views containers, native snapshot fallback, forms and service presentation remain. Full functional migration is incomplete.
Text tiles remain cached per surface. Cost of capturing/rendering a fresh transition surface and possible cache sharing require workload profiling; no performance gain is claimed.
No dependency, crate or framework was added. Metal drawable and QuartzCore delegate APIs use already-linked system frameworks; original-code Apache-2.0 and required upstream notices are unchanged.
